# Plan: Interaction Layer — Wave 2 Gap Closure

## 1. Overview

Waves 1 and 2 of [`interaction_brainstorm.md`](./interaction_brainstorm.md) are implemented and the
full suite is green (12/12 turbo tasks, including lint and prettier). FEAT-032 through FEAT-037 all
landed real code, not stubs: the 17-fixture two-tier gauntlet exists, `HitTargetInterceptorImpl` is
deleted and replaced by exact-point test-and-dispatch, `withAttempts` / `driveWithFallback` /
`withOpenProbe` / `fieldHealingPort` / `mergeLedger` / `mergedAttempts` are all gone, page deltas
ship beside observations, and the vision tool is correctly absent without a grant.

Verification run `20260904T001045Z-do-caa285ca` (2026-09-04, DFW→SJC flights — the same task class
as the Wave 1 evidence run) nonetheless spent **28 turns and 12.9 minutes**, against Wave 2 targets
of **0–2 compensating turns and ≤ 4 minutes**. The Wave 1 evidence run spent 33 turns and 13.2
minutes. On this task class the layer has not moved.

The run is not evidence that Wave 2 was the wrong work — the combobox family, editee resolution,
query shaping, partial-progress batches and deltas all demonstrably worked. It is evidence of
**six defects concentrated in one place: what the layer offers the model when it cannot decide,**
plus one incomplete migration phase. All seven are generic and structural; none needs
site-specific logic.

**The single highest-cost defect, stated plainly:** the calendar reports an ambiguous date by
handing the model two **byte-identical** strings and instructing it to _"re-issue this call with one
of those strings exactly as written."_ There is no string the model can send that resolves the
ambiguity, and the date family has no path that receives an offered label at all. The Wave 1
retype trap has been reproduced in a different widget family, by the same mechanism, past a gate
that was built to prevent exactly this.

**What this plan is not.** It does not revisit anything that works. It adds no new capability
surface, no new tool, and no new dependency. Every change is inside the interaction layer's
existing seams.

## 4. Evidence

All line references verified against the working tree at `d98c985`.

### G1 — Ambiguity offered as indistinguishable strings (FEAT-038)

[`calendar-driver.ts:244-256`](../packages/core/src/widgets/date/calendar-driver.ts#L244-L256):

```ts
const matches = grid.cells.filter((cell) => cell.derivedDate === date);
if (matches.length > 1) {
  return withRead(calendarFailure('WIDGET_AMBIGUOUS_CHOICE', 'several-matched-equally',
    `The calendar exposes ${matches.length} cells for ${date}.`, grid,
    { offered: matches.slice(0, 10).map((cell) => `${cell.monthLabel}: ${cell.name}`) }, ...
```

When two distinct DOM cells carry the same accessible name, `offered` holds the same string twice.
Run seq 11, 25 and 27 each produced:

```
offered: ["2026-12: Monday, December 14, 2026 , 298 US dollars, Cheapest price",
          "2026-12: Monday, December 14, 2026 , 298 US dollars, Cheapest price"]
```

The cells are genuinely distinct elements — `calendar-grid.ts:400,416` dedupes by DOM `path`
before pushing — so this is not double-counting. They are, however, fully distinguishable
**structurally**: `CalendarCell` carries `path`, `selected`, `disabled` and `group`
([`calendar-grid.ts:8-21`](../packages/core/src/widgets/date/calendar-grid.ts#L8-L21)). The driver
discards all of it and asks the model to choose by a label that cannot choose.

The same shape appears at the agent seam: run seq 19 returned
`offered: ["Departure","Departure"]` for `FORM_FIELD_AMBIGUOUS`. That path recovered only because
it also returned `candidates` with distinct refs (`e116`, `e825`) — the pattern this plan
generalizes.

### G2 — The date family emits offered-label advice it cannot receive (FEAT-038)

`selectByOfferedLabel` is defined once, in
[`combobox-driver.ts:281`](../packages/core/src/widgets/combobox/combobox-driver.ts#L281). Three
templates in [`fill/types.ts:219-256`](../packages/core/src/fill/types.ts#L219-L256) declare
`capability: 'selectByOfferedLabel'`, including `WIDGET_AMBIGUOUS_CHOICE/several-matched-equally`,
which the calendar emits.

FEAT-032's capability gate at
[`failure-causes.spec.ts:78-88`](../packages/core/tests/fill/failure-causes.spec.ts#L78-L88)
asserts only:

```ts
expect({ pair, kind: typeof exported[template.capability] }).toEqual({ pair, kind: 'function' });
```

— that a package export of that **name** exists. It cannot see that the family which emitted the
message has no route to it. This is why the gate passed while the trap survived.

Cost in the run: the agent obeyed the hint at seq 13 and seq 29, sending a date-cell label into
`browser_fill_element`. The date driver could not parse it, the value fell through to the
typeahead path, and both calls ended in `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE` after 6.4 s and 5.6 s.

### G3 — Offered lists carry widget chrome, and the resulting advice is destructive (FEAT-038)

[`combobox-driver.ts:450`](../packages/core/src/widgets/combobox/combobox-driver.ts#L450):

```ts
const offered = reaction.candidates.slice(0, MAX_OFFERED).map((candidate) => candidate.name);
```

`collectCandidates` selects on
`'[role="option"],button,a[href],[role="menuitem"],li[onclick],li[tabindex]'`
([`option/candidates.ts:76`](../packages/core/src/widgets/option/candidates.ts#L76)) — bare
`button` included. Against an open date panel that yielded, at run seq 13 and 29:

```
offered: ["Round trip","One way","Reset","Previous","Next",
          "Done. Search for one-way flights, departing on October 9, 2026"]
```

and [`fill/types.ts:227`](../packages/core/src/fill/types.ts#L227) told the model:
_"Re-issue with one of … exactly as written."_ For a **return date** field. Following that advice
with `"One way"` or `"Reset"` would destroy the round-trip search the user asked for.

`PROTECTED_ACTION_RE`
([`interaction/protected-actions.ts:19`](../packages/core/src/interaction/protected-actions.ts#L19))
covers money and commit shapes and correctly does not match these. The gap is not the lexicon: it
is that container **chrome** is being offered as **choices** at all. `WidgetCandidate` already
carries `role`, so the discrimination is available and structural.

### G4 — A fused range failure hides the fields it covered (FEAT-039)

[`browser-fill-form.ts:130`](../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L130)
fuses a date pair into one plan entry. On success the entry discloses what it covered
([line 176](../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L176)):

```ts
applied.push(spec.covers.length > 1 ? { ...outcome, covers: spec.covers } : outcome);
```

`FailedField`
([lines 75-89](../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L75-L89)) has no
`covers` key. In the run, `Departure` and `Return` fused, the fill failed on the return leg, and
the batch reported:

```
failed: [{ field: "Departure", message: "The calendar exposes 2 cells for 2026-12-14." }]
counts: { applied_count: 2, failed_count: 1, skipped_count: 0 }
```

Four fields were requested. `Return` appears in none of `applied`, `failed` or `skipped`,
contradicting the tool's own description
([line 66](../packages/agent/src/adapters/pi/tools/browser-fill-form.ts#L66)), and the `Departure`
failure names the **return** date. The agent then attacked `Return` separately at seq 11–13 down
the same doomed path.

## 6. Security Considerations

> Standing rules in [`memory.md`](./memory.md) → Security. One genuinely new concern.

### FEAT-038: an offered choice is an instruction the agent will follow

The run proves the agent follows offered-label advice literally, including into a dead end. G3
shows the same channel can carry `"One way"` and `"Reset"` to a model filling a return date. An
offered list is therefore not diagnostic output; it is a **menu the agent will pick from**, and it
needs the same care as `browser_click`'s confirmation gateway.

Constraints for the feature spec:

- Offered candidates are filtered structurally to things that are **choices in the container's own
  option semantics**, never arbitrary focusable descendants.
- `PROTECTED_ACTION_RE` applies to offered candidates as it already does to clearance candidates.
  It is necessary, not sufficient: it does not match `"One way"`, which is why the structural rule
  above carries the weight.
- A structural tie-break that clicks a cell the model did not choose is a real action taken on the
  user's behalf. It is permitted only when every surviving candidate is **indistinguishable to the
  model**, the choice is inside the driver's already-resolved container, and the substitution is
  disclosed in the result. Where candidates differ in any model-visible way, the choice stays the
  agent's.
- No offered string is ever synthesized. Every one remains page-derived and passes the same
  sanitizer as any other observation field.

## 7. Architecture & Design (Plan-Specific)

### Why the gate did not catch this, and what changes

`ambiguous-suggestions.html` encodes _"two suggestions match the request equally well"_ with the
labels `"San Jose, CA, United States"` and `"San Jose, Costa Rica"`, driven through the **combobox**
family, with a `followUp` proving the re-issue contract
([`gauntlet.ts:225-243`](../packages/core/tests/support/gauntlet.ts#L225-L243)). That is a correct
and valuable fixture. It cannot fail for G1, G2 or G3, because in it the labels differ, the emitting
family owns `selectByOfferedLabel`, and the container holds nothing but options.

Three properties were being asserted per-fixture that must instead hold **across the catalog**:

1. **Distinctness is a property of the payload, not the prose.** FEAT-032 golden-tests that
   _messages_ are distinct. Nothing tests that the `offered` array a message interpolates has
   distinct members. That check belongs in the catalog contract, where it applies to every template
   with `requiredDetails: ['offered']`.
2. **Capability resolution must be per-emitter, not per-package.** A template naming
   `selectByOfferedLabel` is only honest if the family that can emit it can also receive it. The
   check becomes a mapping from `(surface, family)` to the receiver it exports, so a family
   emitting advice it cannot honor is a compile-or-test failure rather than a run-time dead end.
3. **A hint that names strings must name strings the emitter would accept back.** The strongest
   available form: for every `offered`-bearing template, a fixture in which the advice is actually
   followed and succeeds — the `followUp` mechanism `ambiguous-suggestions` already uses, extended
   to the date family.

Three fixtures make the gate able to see these, all nameable generic patterns:

- **`indistinguishable-choices`** (protocol) — a container offering two enabled, visible controls
  with identical accessible names for the same value. Provenance in the header comment only.
- **`chrome-in-overlay`** (protocol) — a revealed container mixing genuine options with paging and
  mode-switching buttons, at least one of which is destructive relative to the request.
- **`offered-label-roundtrip-date`** (protocol) — the date family's `followUp`: a calendar whose
  ambiguity resolves, and whose offered label, re-issued, commits.

This takes the gate to **20 fixtures**. Per the standing rule, each states its generic pattern; a
site name may appear only as provenance in the header comment.

### The tie-break rule, stated so it cannot become site logic

When several candidates answer the same request, in order:

1. Prefer candidates inside the driver's **already-resolved container**. Scope is structural and
   the driver already holds the container path.
2. Prefer **enabled and visible** over not.
3. Prefer a candidate the page marks `selected` / `aria-selected`.
4. If more than one survives and their **model-visible identities differ**, that is genuine
   ambiguity: report `WIDGET_AMBIGUOUS_CHOICE` with the distinct labels — the existing, correct
   behavior.
5. If more than one survives and their model-visible identities are **identical**, the model cannot
   choose. Take the first in document order, disclose the substitution, and record the count in the
   ledger evidence.

Rule 5 is the whole change. Rules 1–4 are the existing behavior made explicit so the ordering is
testable. No step consults a host, a URL, or a class name.

### Ordering: why choice integrity precedes the accounting cleanup

FEAT-040 is the more principled work and the more invasive. It is second because G1–G3 are
actively producing wrong steering on every run of this task class, while G5–G6 produce _noisy but
harmless_ artifacts. The cost of the ordering is that FEAT-038's new ledger evidence (the
substitution count) is written into the legacy projection first and moved to verdict evidence in
FEAT-040 — one small, named rewrite, accepted deliberately.

## 8. Coding Standards (Plan-Specific Overrides)

**No overrides — see memory.** Two rules are load-bearing here:

- _Never write website-specific automation logic._ Every rule in §7 reads container scope, ARIA
  role, enabled/visible state and document order. A fixture header comment may record which site
  motivated a pattern; nothing else may.
- _Hints may only name engineered capabilities._ FEAT-038 is the mechanical enforcement FEAT-032
  intended, moved from "a function of this name is exported" to "the family that emits this can
  receive it".

## 9. Testing Strategy (Plan-Specific)

- **The three new fixtures gate the features that make them pass**, per the Wave 2 rule. No fixture
  is added that asserts a known unsupported failure.
- **Catalog invariants extend to payloads.** Every template with `requiredDetails: ['offered']`
  gets: offered members are pairwise distinct; the emitting family exports the declared receiver;
  the rendered hint names only members present in `offered`.
- **The tie-break is property-tested.** Over generated candidate sets: a set with any
  model-visible difference never auto-resolves; a fully identical set always resolves to document
  order and always discloses; a candidate outside the resolved container is never chosen.
- **The destructive-advice case is asserted by name.** A container mixing options with a
  mode-switching control never offers that control, and the assertion names the control.
- **FEAT-039 asserts set completeness**, not counts: every requested field name appears in exactly
  one of `applied` / `failed` / `skipped`, for the fused and unfused paths, on success and failure.
- **FEAT-040's shared state is asserted at the seam, not the unit.** `chargedActions` after a
  multi-rung combobox fill equals the counting port's real mutation count for the whole call, and
  `remainingActions` decreases monotonically across nesting. The 20 fixtures keep their pinned
  `expectedMutations` / `expectedReads` — the proof this changes attribution, not work.
- **The boundary rule gains the three symbols it cannot currently see**: `queryRecord`, `renumber`,
  and `toLegacyLedger` on the fill path.
- **No always-empty field may be serialized.** A contract test over a real failing fill asserts
  `details.attempted[]` contains no key whose value is `[]`, `0`, or `null` for every record.
- **Fixture paths resolve from `import.meta.url`**, never `process.cwd()`.
- **Vision stays non-load-bearing.** The 20 fixtures must pass with vision disabled.

## 10. Logging Strategy (Plan-Specific)

> Standing conventions in [`memory.md`](./memory.md) → Logging. No new sink.

- **FEAT-038** — the substitution rides the existing sanitized ledger as rung evidence: how many
  candidates were indistinguishable and which position was taken. Filtered-out chrome is not logged
  as page text; only the count is.
- **FEAT-039** — `covers` is a field-name list already present in the call's own input. No new
  page-derived data.
- **FEAT-040** — the ledger becomes the projection FEAT-034 specified. `entry_evidence` carries the
  query form for WHAT rungs and the entry condition for others, bounded and sanitized at the agent
  seam.

## 12. Decisions Closed by This Plan

1. **Indistinguishable candidates are not ambiguity.** Asking the model to choose between identical
   strings is a defect, not a conservative default. The engine resolves and discloses.
2. **Offered lists are menus, not diagnostics.** They are filtered structurally and vetoed by
   `PROTECTED_ACTION_RE`, and only genuine options qualify.
3. **Capability resolution is per-family.** A package-level export check is insufficient and is
   replaced, not supplemented.
4. **No new tool, flag, preference or dependency.** Every gap is closed inside existing seams.
5. **FEAT-034 phase 3 is reopened rather than re-specified.** Its TASK-004 and TASK-010 contracts
   were correct; the migration stopped short of them and completes here.
